title: A Look at Assassinorum Execution Force, from Games Workshop
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v-ylvHTi_Mc

Daniel (@dungeondive) returns to science fiction with Assassinorum: Execution Force, a co-op Games Workshop board game of infiltration in the 41st millennium. Four assassins (Vindicare, Eversor, Callidus and Culexus) creep through a cultist base hunting for a control panel and a teleporter, then jump into the Astropathic Sanctum to kill a Chaos Sorcerer Lord before his ritual completes at the end of round twelve. The Eversor can self-destruct and win the game in the blast.

He bought it cheaply on eBay years ago, without the four assassin minis, back when sellers were splitting the box. The production is classic GW, and the lore pages, including a two-page spread for each assassin, carry much of the appeal. Rooms are drawn when an assassin gains line of sight, and they spawn cultists stunned in surprise. Alerted enemies follow patrol arrows, rolling a d6 at junctions, a system he likes from Dungeon Crusade. An event deck that draws more cards for every alerted foe throws random sweeps and patrols into the plan.

His verdict is "okay." It's quick, easy to relearn and easy to run solo, but low on tension, which the optional achievements try to fix. He wants one more layer of complexity, and assassin cards twice the size so he isn't always flipping them. Don't pay eBay prices, he says, though $20 without the minis would be fine with proxies.

----

Execution Force keeps its shelf space by being quick to relearn. How much do you value a game you can set up in minutes over one with more depth?
